    Injectivity of dimension-vector maps on torsion-class Grothendieck monoids #

    Theorem 4.1 (thm:mon-dim, condition (mon-dim) in Theorem A(I)) of the manuscript:

    • torsionMonoid_injective_of_equalClassHom: under (K₀-Hom), pushing out short exact sequences along nonzero morphisms between modules of equal class shows by induction on length that M(T) → K₀(mod R) is injective for every torsion class T.
    • isEFinite_iff_injective_weakTorsionMonoid and isEFinite_iff_injective_torsionMonoid: conversely, two nonisomorphic g-stable bricks of equal class have distinct classes in the Grothendieck monoid of the weak g-semistable torsion class, completing (E-fin) ⇔ (mon-dim).

    Function.Injective ⇑(GrothendieckMonoid.dimensionMap T)

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.isEFinite_iff_injective_torsionMonoid {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsArtinianRing R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] :
    IsEFinite R ↔ ∀ (T : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat R)), T.IsClosedUnderQuotients → T.IsClosedUnderExtensions → T 0 → Function.Injective ⇑(GrothendieckMonoid.dimensionMap T)

    Injectivity of the ambient class map for every torsion class characterizes E-finiteness. A torsion class in the finite module category contains zero and is closed under quotients and extensions.
